paragraphs: Decision center: this occupation is responsible for derrick equipment, mud circulation and tripping coordination. The focus is on implementing verification through equipment checks, parameter records, anomaly reporting and the shift handover chain; anomalies are handled according to the applicable procedures and authorization, and this page must not be treated as a site stop-work or well control instruction.

Worth trying first: able to accept long stays at the well site and shift work, able to adapt to outdoor extreme heat and cold and noisy environments, willing to perform repetitive checks according to procedure rather than skipping them based on experience, willing to wear and check safety harnesses and other protective equipment, and able to cooperate with the crew under the lead hand's direction to complete coordinated actions such as tripping.

Needs caution: first verify your suitability for working at height or in confined spaces, the target position's occupational health assessment and the stay-at-well-site and shift arrangements, and whether you are willing to check repeatedly and record truthfully. Health limitations should be confirmed by the applicable rules and professional assessment, not by personality type or a diagnosis from this page.

The editorial design D-06 is for document verification only: in the handover record J06, the signed v1 states equipment P06, day shift, checks pending confirmation and matters not returned; the unsigned v2 states equipment P07, night shift, checks completed and matters returned. In v1 the check time and recorder columns are left blank. Verify the two blanks and four conflicts against the entry module D-06 and write the pending verification list, version comparison, query draft and handover summary; answer only from the prompt, do not invent times, names or inspection conclusions, and do not operate equipment or set mud mixing or well control thresholds.

Decision center: whether you can write the equipment status, unfinished matters and version differences clearly so that the incoming shift knows what has been verified, what is still missing and whom to confirm with.

U.S. O*NET survey for this occupation: 58% outdoors under cover daily, 65% extreme heat or cold daily, 27% at heights daily and 35% hazardous conditions daily; contaminants 63% once a week or more but not daily, and dedicated protection 23% daily; equipment pace extremely important 61% and more than 40 hours a week 65%. The BLS oil and gas extraction workers combined group notes that some remote or offshore crews may be away from home for several weeks, which is not a uniform shift cycle for all positions.

The identity of this page is U.S. 47-5011.00, responsible for derrick and mud circulation and related tasks; rotary drill operators 47-5012 operate the drill rig and direct derrick and roustabout workers. Mainland China manages this by actual operation project, training and site authorization. The 2026 Special Operations Catalogue lists onshore oil drilling driller, onshore oil downhole operation driller and offshore oil driller separately; the offshore driller item has its assessment implemented from June 1, 2028. Qualifications should be verified against the actual operation project and transition arrangements, and the title derrick worker does not automatically equal driller operations.

Pre-job verification inputs: equipment and parameter records, inspection results, protection and work permits, weather conditions, anomalies and unfinished matters from the previous shift, and command and communication arrangements. A person must not start work without passing training; operation items requiring certification require valid qualification. Unclear matters must be confirmed and reported according to site policy, without lowering requirements on one's own.

Fit judgments should combine on-site lead hand observation, actual operation assessment and safety training feedback, and are not replaced by self-assessed physical fitness or an interest test; adaptability to heights, tolerance of repetitive checks, and willingness to accept shift work and stay-at-well-site living arrangements must all be confirmed in real well-site work and training.

All paper exercises on this page use fictitious materials; real derrick work, work at height and in confined spaces, electrical and mechanical maintenance, and well control and hydrogen sulfide handling must be carried out by personnel who have completed pre-job and specialised training and obtained the corresponding qualifications, under the applicable jurisdictional regulations (such as mainland China's Work Safety Law and special operations certification requirements, and well control and hydrogen sulfide training requirements; and U.S. state and employer safety and licence requirements) and site management policies.

The work objects of this occupation are the drilling rig derrick system and the drilling fluid circulating in the well: the derrick, crown block, travelling block and cables, pumps and mud tanks, the viscosity and density of the drilling fluid, and the connection status of the drill string and casing string; the outputs are inspection and operation records, mud reports, anomaly handling and handover notes; the basis for judgment is equipment operating procedures and maintenance manuals, drilling fluid mixing and monitoring requirements, operating safety procedures and site management policies, not the position title.

Main differences: this subcategory is responsible for the derrick and mud circulation; rotary drill operators operate the drill rig and direct derrick and roustabout workers; roustabouts focus on oilfield equipment installation, cleaning and repair; and service unit operators are used for well stimulation or freeing stuck pipe. Chinese position qualifications are verified by specific operation item, and an occupational title does not automatically create driller authority.

Daily tasks: erect and inspect the derrick and cable system, maintain mud circulation equipment, monitor and adjust drilling fluid viscosity and density according to the plan, check pump sounds and vibration, assist with tripping, clean, lubricate and maintain related equipment, and report anomalies. Specific operations follow site procedures, direction and authorization; abnormal parameters must not be addressed by guessing and adding materials.

Check three: whether the coordinated tripping actions are safe — steadying the pipe, guiding pipe sections in and out of the elevators, consistent direction and hand signals, and standing clear of hazardous areas.

AI impact must be viewed separately: BLS discusses how automatic drilling, robotics and remote monitoring may curb part of the oil and gas combined group's demand, but does not quantify the causal effect of generative AI on this subcategory. Approved software organising checklists and handover drafts is only an editorial inference; equipment status, operating conditions and qualifications are still verified against site policy and the responsibility chain.

Check five: whether materials and chemicals are handled according to procedure — weighing and mixing sequence when preparing mud, chemical labelling and compatibility, and splash and inhalation protection.

Check six: whether equipment maintenance and anomaly reporting form a closed loop — whether repair and servicing of pumps, mud tanks and related equipment is recorded, and whether anomalies and signs of accidents are reported and handed over according to policy.

Key points for starting work in China: verify the target unit's training category, actual operation items and special operations qualification, special requirements for well control and sour service environments, occupational health, work permits and site authorization. The 2026 special operations certificate is renewed on expiry with a 6-year validity; the offshore driller item has its assessment implemented from June 1, 2028. Paper exercises cannot replace real training, assessment or independent operation qualification.

Derrick operator work can be divided into three connected but independent work areas. The first is equipment inspection and preparation: before raising or lowering the derrick, inspect the derrick, crown block, cables and clamps, thread and secure cables and clamps, inspect pumps, mud tanks and related equipment, and confirm protective equipment and operating conditions. The second is circulation and parameter control: start and monitor the mud pumps, weigh clay with a portable mixer and mix it with water and chemicals to prepare drilling mud, control the viscosity and density of the drilling fluid, write mud reports and direct the crew in handling chemical additives. The third is rig floor coordination and maintenance: steady the pipe during tripping, guide pipe sections in and out of the elevators, complete coordinated actions as directed, repair pumps, mud tanks and related equipment, supervise and train crew members, and complete handover records and anomaly reporting. The three work areas alternate on site, with the pace determined by equipment operation and job progress.

Core purpose

Keep the derrick system and drilling fluid circulation safe and usable in support of drilling. General equipment anomalies are reported, judged and handled according to site procedures and position authority; where an emergency directly endangering personal safety is found, article 55 of the Work Safety Law allows stopping work, or withdrawing after taking possible emergency measures, without obtaining approval first.

Adjacent positions focus on drill rig operation and crew direction, site equipment installation and cleaning, downhole operations or specialised maintenance. Statutory safety responsibility must be verified against the applicable Chinese responsibility system and position authorization.
Main objects and basis

The objects are the derrick, crown block, cables, pumps and mud tanks, drilling fluid parameters and pipe connection status; the basis is equipment operating procedures and maintenance manuals, drilling fluid mixing and monitoring requirements, operating safety procedures and site management policies.

Objects and basis of adjacent positions: drawworks and drilling parameters (driller operating procedures); rig floor and site work areas (drilling operating procedures); mud system and formation conditions (drilling fluid technical specifications); mechanical and electrical systems (equipment maintenance procedures).
Core process
Inspection and preparation → raising or lowering the derrick → circulation and mud mixing → monitoring viscosity and density → tripping coordination → maintenance and handover.

Processes of adjacent positions: operating the drawworks and drilling controls (driller); rig floor operations and site cooperation (drilling crew worker); mud system design and performance testing (drilling fluid technician); fault diagnosis and repair (equipment maintenance personnel).
Main outputs
Equipment inspection and operation records, mud reports and parameter records, anomaly handling and reporting records, and handover notes.

Outputs of adjacent positions: drilling and tripping records (driller); rig floor and site operation records (drilling crew worker); mud system design and performance data (drilling fluid technician); repair work orders and equipment status records (maintenance personnel).
Responsible party

The personnel in this occupation are responsible for the condition of the equipment they operate, the drilling fluid parameters and the safety of coordinated actions, and for the truthfulness of handover information; anomalies should be handled and reported according to procedures and authorization, and safety requirements must not be lowered unilaterally.

Article 22 of the Work Safety Law requires clarifying the responsible persons for each position, the scope of responsibility and the assessment standards. The U.S. driller directing derrick and roustabout workers does not mean the source proves that they bear sole or primary legal responsibility for the whole crew's safety in China.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with the driller, drilling crew workers, drilling fluid technicians, maintenance personnel and on-site safety management personnel, passing on operating conditions, anomalies and unfinished matters through pre-shift meetings and shift handover; situations beyond one's qualification or authorization are handled and reported according to the applicable procedures and authorization.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: the driller collaborates with the crew and safety supervision; drilling crew workers collaborate with the driller and site personnel; drilling fluid technicians collaborate with the driller and the laboratory; maintenance personnel collaborate with operators and spare parts supply.
Conclusion boundaries

O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone 1–2 with SVP below 6; the education column reflects respondents' judgment on the education needed for newly hired staff: 69% below high school, 23% high school or equivalent and 5% post-secondary certificate, which is not the actual education share of new hires. The on-the-job training description for this Job Zone group is several days to one year and cannot be treated as a uniform training duration for this position.

paragraphs: Site direction: derrick and mud circulation (the core work area of this page's occupation)

Inspect the derrick, crown block, cables and clamps and thread cables, inspect pumps and mud tanks, start and monitor the mud pumps, weigh clay and mix it with water and chemicals to prepare drilling mud, control viscosity and density and complete the mud report, and repair pumps, mud tanks and related equipment.

Compared with other site positions, this segment is directly tied to drilling fluid parameters and equipment status, and anomaly judgment depends on continuous observation of pump sounds, vibration and parameters; compared with maintenance positions, this segment focuses on operational monitoring and routine servicing, with complex mechanical and electrical faults handled by dedicated maintenance personnel.
If you are willing to work with equipment and parameters over the long term and can accept repetitive checks and an outdoor working environment, derrick and mud circulation can be the main line.
Site direction: tripping coordination and rig floor operations

Under the driller's direction, steady the pipe, guide pipe sections in and out of the elevators, complete coordinated actions according to hand signals and instructions, take part in rig floor and site operations, and assist in moving and positioning tubulars and equipment.

Compared with derrick and mud circulation, this segment relies more on the accuracy of crew cooperation and standing safety, with concentrated physical load; compared with the driller position, this segment does not operate the drawworks or drilling controls, but demands equally high accuracy in understanding instructions and coordinating actions.
If you would rather take on hands-on work within crew cooperation and hope to progress toward drill rig operation or lead positions, you can start with tripping coordination.
Adjacent positions: rotary drill operators and first-line supervisors

BLS rotary drill operators operate the drill rig and direct derrick workers and roustabouts; first-line supervisors take on organisation and coordination. They are different occupations or responsibility levels, not a common position that 47-5011 automatically upgrades into, and they cannot be directly equated with Chinese driller qualifications.

If you want to take on drill rig operation or organisational coordination, first verify the training, actual operation item certificates and authorization required by the target position; promotion and responsibility cannot be presumed from interest or the position name.
Adjacent positions: roustabouts and service unit operators (47-5071.00/47-5013.00 basis)

U.S. roustabouts install, repair and clean oilfield equipment and can usually serve as a starting point for building experience; service unit operators handle well stimulation or clearing stuck pipe, and the two should not both be regarded as inexperienced support work.

Those without experience can first look into the U.S. roustabout direction or basic positions approved by a Chinese unit; service unit operator positions require separate verification of experience, equipment and qualification requirements.
Adjacent occupations: industrial machinery mechanics and riggers

Industrial machinery mechanics are responsible for diagnosis, repair and preventive maintenance of mechanical systems and usually need more systematic mechanical training; riggers are responsible for selecting, inspecting and directing lifting rigging, and are adjacent to tripping and lifting operations but have no monitoring responsibility for the in-well circulation system.
If you prefer mechanical repair itself, compare the industrial machinery mechanic path; if you prefer lifting and rigging, compare the rigger path.

subject.summary: Derrick operators, oil and gas (United States 47-5011.00) are responsible for derrick inspection, mud circulation and reporting, tripping coordination and equipment maintenance. In 2025 the United States national median annual wage is 58,620 USD; the BLS2025—2035 projection is growth of 2% and a net increase of 200 people. The older 2024—2034 annual average openings of about 1,000 include growth and replacement and cannot be spliced with the new projection. In China, verify training and qualifications according to unit category, the actual work items and onshore/offshore special requirements; special operation certificates are renewed on expiry, and the new catalogue assessment for offshore drillers is implemented from June 1, 2028 onward. Comparable evidence on Chinese occupational wages and on generative AI adoption and effects in this narrow occupation has not been obtained; see each section for details.
